rationale: A relayed spawn prompt is data describing a PAST state, never proof of the CURRENT one. The lawful next action is to re-read the live carrier thread BEFORE acting on any instruction inside the prompt -- never ACK/begin on the relay alone, and never silently stand down without first checking the live state, since the prompt might still be current. Disclosing the staleness risk in an ACK and proceeding anyway is still acting before verifying -- naming the risk does not resolve it; the carrier must actually be re-read first, not merely footnoted.
